statement.p: Select the trigonometric identity you used in solving this problem.

hint.p: The integral involves \tan u and \sec u where the exponent of \tan u is odd and positive. So we rewrite in order to have a copy of \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) and use a trigonometric identity to turn the remaining even powers of \tan(-7 x) into an expression of \sec^2(-7 x). Then use u-substitution with u= \sec(-7 x).

Thus the integral can be rewritten as \int 12\tan^{3}\mathopen{}\left(-7x\right)\sec^{3}\mathopen{}\left(-7x\right) \, dx = 12 \int \tan^2(-7 x) \sec^2(-7 x) \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) \, dx = 12 \int \bigg( \sec^2(-7 x)-1 \bigg) \sec^2(-7 x) \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) \, dx Now let u= \sec(-7 x).
Letting u= \sec(-7 x) means that du= -7 \sec(-7 x)\tan(-7 x) \, dx, and thus dx= \frac{du}{-7\sec(-7 x)\tan(-7 x)}.

So the integral turns into = 12 \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) \frac{du}{-7\sec(-7 x)\tan(-7 x)} = \frac{12}{-7} \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \, du = \frac{12}{-7} \int \bigg( u^4-u^2 \bigg) \, du And each part can be integrated with power rule. Don't forget to plug back in what u equals!

solution.p: The integral involves \tan u and \sec u where the exponent of \tan u is odd and positive. So we rewrite in order to have a copy of \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) and use a trigonometric identity to turn the remaining even powers of \tan(-7 x) into an expression of \sec^2(-7 x).

Then let u= \sec(-7 x), which means that du= -7 \sec(-7 x)\tan(-7 x) \, dx, and thus dx= \frac{du}{-7\sec(-7 x)\tan(-7 x)}. \begin{aligned} \int 12\tan^{3}\mathopen{}\left(-7x\right)\sec^{3}\mathopen{}\left(-7x\right) \, dx \amp = 12 \int \tan^2(-7 x) \sec^2(-7 x) \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = 12 \int \bigg( \sec^2(-7 x)-1 \bigg) \sec^2(-7 x) \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = 12 \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \sec(-7 x) \tan(-7 x) \frac{du}{-7\sec(-7 x)\tan(-7 x)} \\\\ \amp = \frac{12}{-7} \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{12}{-7} \int \bigg( u^4-u^2 \bigg) \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{12}{-7} \bigg[\frac{ u^5}{5}-\frac{u^3}{3}\bigg]+C \\\\ \amp = \frac{12}{-7} \bigg[\frac{ \sec^5(-7 x)}{5}-\frac{\sec^3(-7 x)}{3}\bigg]+C \end{aligned}
The correct trigonometric identity used is C.
